0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 25 July 1977, after the draft finalized by the Travel Requisites Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council.
0.2 Suitcases used for air travel differ in design, shape, colour and size from Even with a particular size and shape, the one manufacturer to another. quality of the material and workmanship may be different. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, due weightage has been given to the proper type of materials to be used and prevalent trade practices being followed by the manufacturers in this field. 0.4 The size specified in this standard would cater to the requirements of majority of users and will also be suitable for the space available in aeroplane. 0.5 This standard contains clauses which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier and which permit the buyer to use his option for selection to suit his requirements. The clauses are 2.2, 4.4, 4.5,4.8,5.2, 7.1 and 9.1. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960+. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements leather cloth for use in air travel.

IS : 85-18 - 1977 4. CONSTRUCTION 4.1 The suitcase shall be soundly constructed.
fastened by means of fastener 4.2 The handles body. shall be reinforced The two portions on all the three sides. with vulcanized shall be

fibre and riveted to the

4.3 The handles with the fittings and attachments shall be strong and shall The not yield under normal usage. The handles shall be centrally located. clearance between the body of the suitcase and the inner faces of the handles shall be adequate to facilitate easy gripping, when lifted. 4.4 Certain other provisions such as inside compartments, and alternate arrangements may also be provided as agreed purchaser and the supplier. pockets, locks to between the

The partitions shall be of leather cloth 4.5 The suitcase shall be flexible. or leather as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. There may be 2 to 3 compartments. 4.6 The stitches shall be strong and uniform. Waxed thread shall be used for stitching. The stitches shall be of lock stitch with 28 to 32 numbers The stitch ends shall be secured either per decimetre and of even tension. by knotting the thread or back stitching or by an additional row of stitching. 4.7 The leather used for the body of the suitcase shall be 1.5 to 2 mm in The finish of leather shall be top thickness and 1.5 mm for the partition. grain, plane or embossed. 4.8 The slide fasteners used for the outside closure of the suitcase shall be of heavy quality and for inside compartments, pockets, etc, shall be of medium or light quality as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 5. 5.4 In respect of appearance, general workmanship and finish, the suitcases shall conform to the sample previously approved by the consumer. 6. TESTS 6.1 Handle Snatch Test - The air travel suitcase shall be securely fixed in an inverted position on a rigid support, leading the handle free for applying the load. The handle shall be suitably harnessed to distribute the A load of 100 N ( 10 kgf ) shall be load applied over the entire handle. applied suddenly to the handle and repeated 10 times. 6.1.1 The weight may be applied either by means of a spring balance or weights, suitably placed on stirrup. During or after the test, the handles shall not have snapped or shall not have loosened in fittings. 6.2 Drop Test - The air travel suitcase shall be filled with cloths and papers or other suitable materials to the full, subject to the total contents to weigh 50 & 2.5 N ( 5 & 0.25 kgf). The suitcase shall be locked after filling the specified weight. The suitcase shall be dropped from a height of 1 m on a wooden floor or on a board for 10 times. The suitcase shall not be damaged or get splits. During or after the test the contents shall not show out. 7. SAMPLING 7.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the procedure given in IS : 2500 ( Part I )-1973" shall be followed for sampling plan as given in 7.2, 7.2.1 and 7.3. 7.2 The scale of sampling shall correspond to inspection level III given in Table 1 of IS : 2500 ( Part I )-1973* for all requirements specified in the standard except handle snatch test (~6,l ) and drop test ( 6.2 ). 7.2.1 For handle snatch test and drop test, the scale of sampling shall correspond to inspection level II given in Table 1 of IS : 2500 (Part I )1973*. 7.3 The sampling plan shall correspond Table 2 of IS : 2500 (Part I )-1973'. 8. MARKING 8.1 Each air travel suitcase shall be clearly and permanently the following: a) Manufacturer's name or registered trade-mark; and b) Size of the suitcase.

Certifica-

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard made thereunder. conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

9. -PACKING 9.1 The air travel suitcase shall be packed to ensure safe transportation. They may also be packed as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser.
